summary: Dear NOVA is a browser-based space mission game that takes players from mission design to mission operation. In Act 0, the player prepares the crewed Mars ship Odyssey-1 by splitting limited points between fuel, hull armor, science payload and summon capacitors. Those choices matter in flight: the player then pilots the ship in real-time 3D through a debris field, a Mars arrival and a descent to Jezero Crater while watching hull, fuel, charges and trust on a live dashboard. The twist is NOVA, the ship's voice AI co-pilot. Players speak or type requests such as repair drones, supply crates or navigation beacons, and NOVA grants, refuses or twists them, while balance rules and limited charges keep the AI from breaking the game. Four endings show how well the player balanced risk, resources and trust. It runs on phones and laptops, works without a microphone, needs no login and is open source. The Mars mission is built around NASA reference facts on launch windows, transfer time and Jezero Crater.

PROJECT DETAILS (rich-text box; make the capitalized lines bold)

WHAT IT IS Dear NOVA turns the Space Mission Design challenge into a game that runs from mission design to mission operation. The player is the Commander of Odyssey-1, a crewed Mars transport, and shares the ship with NOVA, an experimental voice AI who can reshape the space around you.

HOW IT ANSWERS THE CHALLENGE

  • Design (Act 0): a loadout screen where the player splits limited points between Fuel Tank, Hull Armor, Science Payload and Summon Capacitors. More of one means less of another, and the choice carries into flight.
  • Operation (Acts 1, 3 and 4): a real-time 3D flight through a debris field, a Mars arrival and descent gates, and a landing at Jezero Crater with rover deployment and science telemetry sent back to Earth.
  • Live resources: hull, fuel, summon charges and trust are shown on a cockpit dashboard and drive the outcome.
  • Consequences: unexpected hazards (asteroid clusters, space junk) and limited charges mean every decision costs something. Four different endings reflect how the player managed risk, resources and trust.
  • Repeatable: players can replay with a different loadout and strategy.

THE AI CO-PILOT (THE CREATIVE IDEA) Players talk to NOVA by voice or text: "NOVA, repair the hull." NOVA grants, grants with a cost, twists, refuses or pranks, depending on a trust meter. Her requests are mapped to a bounded set of in-game objects (repair drone, supply crate, escort fighter, beacon, wormhole shortcut) with charge limits, a cap of 12 live objects and safe spawn distances, so the AI can be playful without breaking the simulation. A deterministic rules engine validates every AI action and takes over if the AI service is unavailable.

ACCESSIBILITY AND RELIABILITY Three voice paths (offline wake word, browser speech recognition, recorded-audio fallback) plus a text bar and quick-command chips, so the whole game is playable without a microphone. Desktop and mobile controls. [45 automated unit and integration tests pass.]

NASA SCIENCE REFERENCES The mission is built around real NASA facts: Earth-Mars launch windows recur about every 26 months (the synodic period, about 780 days); a minimum-energy transfer takes about 6 to 9 months; the landing site is Jezero Crater, explored by the Perseverance rover; the ship concept references NASA's Deep Space Transport idea. Sources are listed in the NASA Data field.

TOOLS React, Three.js with React Three Fiber, TypeScript, Zustand, Tailwind CSS, Vite, Vercel serverless functions, Google Gemini API, Vosk (offline speech model), Web Speech API, Web Audio API. Open source under the MIT licence.

WHAT WE SIMPLIFIED, AND WHAT IS NOT IN THIS VERSION Flight physics are arcade-scale for playability; NASA facts shape the mission, but this is not a full orbital simulation. The dashboard tracks four resources (hull, fuel, charges, trust), not a full mass, power, budget, data, communications and time model. Act 2 (Transit Corridor) is planned and not part of this build. NOVA's AI responses can vary, which is why a rules engine checks every action.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) ACKNOWLEDGMENT SI is part of the product: NOVA's replies and actions are generated at runtime by Google Gemini through function calling, then validated by our rules engine, with a scripted fallback when no key is available. NOVA's spoken lines use the browser's speech synthesis (a synthetic voice).
